<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<title>Byufuel — how the product works</title>
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;500&family=IBM+Plex+Sans:wght@400;500;600&display=swap">
<style>
:root{
  --bg:#E7F0EC; --surface:#FFFFFF; --ink:#13211C; --ink-2:#3E524B; --ink-3:#5E726B;
  --rule:#D3E0DA; --accent:#0B6A62; --accent-deep:#084E48; --accent-soft:#E3F4F1;
  --blue:#1D4E89; --blue-bg:#EAF2FB; --blue-line:#B7D0EE;
  --amber:#8A5A09; --amber-bg:#FBF3E4; --amber-line:#E4C98A;
  --pass:#1F7A3A; --pass-bg:#E5F6EB; --fail:#A33B2C; --fail-bg:#FDECEA;
  --known:#8A5A09; --known-bg:#FBF3E4; --code:#E8F3EF;
  --sans:"IBM Plex Sans",-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"Segoe UI",Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;
  --mono:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace;
}
*{box-sizing:border-box}
html{scroll-behavior:smooth}
body{margin:0;background:linear-gradient(180deg,#D7EBE4 0,#E7F0EC 220px);color:var(--ink);font-family:var(--sans);font-size:16px;line-height:1.6;-webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased}
.wrap{max-width:1000px;margin:0 auto;padding:28px 20px 80px}
h1{font-size:32px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.02em;margin:0 0 8px;text-wrap:balance;color:#fff}
h2{font-size:22px;font-weight:600;margin:0;letter-spacing:-.01em;display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:10px}
h2::before{content:"";width:8px;height:22px;border-radius:4px;background:var(--accent);flex:none}
h3{font-size:16px;font-weight:600;margin:8px 0 0;color:var(--accent-deep)}
p{margin:0}
.lede{color:rgba(255,255,255,.92);max-width:68ch;font-size:16.5px}
.lede + .lede{margin-top:8px}
.meta{margin-top:14px;color:rgba(255,255,255,.78);font-size:13.5px}
header{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#084E48 0%,#0B6A62 55%,#1A8F7A 100%);border-radius:18px;padding:28px 26px 22px;box-shadow:0 10px 28px rgba(8,78,72,.22)}
.logo-plate{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;background:#fff;border-radius:12px;padding:10px 16px;margin-bottom:18px}
.logo{height:46px;width:auto;display:block}
.eyebrow{margin:0 0 4px;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:rgba(255,255,255,.75)}
section{margin-top:22px;display:grid;gap:14px;scroll-margin-top:96px;min-width:0;background:var(--surface);border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:16px;padding:22px 22px 24px;box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(19,33,28,.04)}
#product{border-top:4px solid var(--accent)}
#flow{border-top:4px solid var(--blue)}
#flow h2::before{background:var(--blue)}
#setup{border-top:4px solid #3D6B9A}
#setup h2::before{background:#3D6B9A}
#users{border-top:4px solid #2F6B4F}
#users h2::before{background:#2F6B4F}
#tested{border-top:4px solid var(--pass)}
#tested h2::before{background:var(--pass)}
#failing{border-top:4px solid var(--fail)}
#failing h2::before{background:var(--fail)}
#gaps{border-top:4px solid var(--amber)}
#gaps h2::before{background:var(--amber)}
#creds{border-top:4px solid #6B3FA0}
#creds h2::before{background:#6B3FA0}
.phase{background:#F7FBFA;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-left:5px solid var(--accent);border-radius:12px;padding:16px 18px;display:grid;gap:10px;scroll-margin-top:96px;min-width:0}
#flow-supplier{background:var(--blue-bg);border-color:var(--blue-line);border-left-color:var(--blue)}
#flow-supplier h3,#flow-supplier .kicker{color:var(--blue)}
#flow-admin{background:#F3FAF8;border-color:#B7DDD4;border-left-color:var(--accent)}
#flow-tsm{background:var(--amber-bg);border-color:var(--amber-line);border-left-color:var(--amber)}
#flow-tsm h3,#flow-tsm .kicker{color:var(--amber)}
#flow-wh{background:#F4F7FB;border-color:#C5D4EA;border-left-color:#3D6B9A}
#flow-wh h3,#flow-wh .kicker{color:#3D6B9A}
.subtoc{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px}
.subtoc a{font-size:13.5px;font-weight:600;text-decoration:none;color:var(--blue);border:1px solid var(--blue-line);padding:8px 14px;border-radius:999px;background:#fff}
.subtoc a:hover,.subtoc a:focus-visible{color:#fff;border-color:var(--blue);background:var(--blue)}
.phase h3{margin:0}
.kicker{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent)}
.sec-sub{color:var(--ink-2);max-width:74ch}
code{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:.86em;background:var(--code);color:var(--accent-deep);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:4px;border:1px solid #C9E3DC}
a{color:var(--accent-deep)}
header a{color:#fff;text-decoration:underline}
:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px}

.toc{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;margin-top:14px;position:sticky;top:0;z-index:5;background:#E7F0EC;padding:10px 2px;border-bottom:1px solid #C5DDD4}
.toc a{font-size:13.5px;font-weight:600;text-decoration:none;color:var(--accent-deep);border:1px solid transparent;padding:8px 14px;border-radius:999px;background:#fff;cursor:pointer;box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(8,78,72,.08)}
.toc a:hover,.toc a:focus-visible{color:#fff;background:var(--accent);border-color:var(--accent)}

.callout{display:grid;gap:4px;padding:14px 16px;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #B7DDD4;background:var(--accent-soft);border-left:5px solid var(--accent)}
.callout strong{font-weight:600;color:var(--accent-deep)}
.callout.ok{border-color:#B7E0C4;background:var(--pass-bg);border-left-color:var(--pass)}
.callout.ok strong{color:var(--pass)}
.callout.warn{border-color:var(--amber-line);background:var(--amber-bg);border-left-color:var(--amber)}
.callout.warn strong{color:var(--amber)}

.flow{background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:12px;padding:16px;display:grid;gap:14px}
.lane{display:grid;gap:8px}
.lane-name{font-size:12px;color:#fff;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.06em;font-weight:600;background:var(--accent);display:inline-block;width:max-content;padding:3px 10px;border-radius:999px}
#flow-supplier .lane-name{background:var(--blue)}
#flow-tsm .lane-name{background:var(--amber)}
#flow-wh .lane-name{background:#3D6B9A}
.steps{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(180px,1fr));gap:10px;align-items:stretch}
.step{min-width:0;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-top:4px solid var(--accent);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 12px;background:#fff;display:grid;gap:3px;align-content:start}
#flow-supplier .step{border-top-color:var(--blue)}
#flow-tsm .step{border-top-color:var(--amber)}
#flow-wh .step{border-top-color:#3D6B9A}
.step b{font-size:14px;font-weight:600}
.step span{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--ink-2)}
.arrow{display:none}
.step.ok{border-color:#8FCB9F;border-top-color:var(--pass);background:var(--pass-bg)}
.step.no{border-color:#F0B2A8;border-top-color:var(--fail);background:var(--fail-bg)}
.tbl{overflow-x:auto;max-width:100%;min-width:0;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:12px;background:#fff}
table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:14px}
th,td{text-align:left;padding:10px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule);vertical-align:top}
th{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:#fff;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.04em;background:var(--accent-deep)}
#failing th{background:var(--fail)}
#gaps th{background:#7A4E08}
#creds th{background:#5B348C}
#tested th{background:var(--pass)}
#users th{background:#245C40}
tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:#F4FAF8}
#failing tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:#FFF6F4}
#gaps tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:#FBF7EF}
#creds tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:#F7F3FB}
tr:last-child td{border-bottom:0}
td.num{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;text-align:right;font-weight:600;color:var(--accent-deep)}

.pill{display:inline-block;font:600 12px var(--sans);padding:2px 8px;border-radius:999px;white-space:nowrap}
.p-pass{color:#146332;background:var(--pass-bg);border:1px solid #B7E0C4}
.p-fail{color:#8E2E22;background:var(--fail-bg);border:1px solid #F0B2A8}
.p-known{color:#7A4E08;background:var(--known-bg);border:1px solid var(--amber-line)}
.p-acc{color:var(--accent-deep);background:var(--accent-soft);border:1px solid #B7DDD4}
.scores{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px}
.scores .pill{font-size:13px;padding:6px 10px}

ol.clean{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none;display:grid;gap:10px;color:var(--ink-2);counter-reset:step}
ol.clean li{position:relative;margin:0;padding:2px 0 2px 40px}
ol.clean li::before{counter-increment:step;content:counter(step);position:absolute;left:0;top:0;width:28px;height:28px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--accent);color:#fff;font-size:13px;font-weight:600;line-height:28px;text-align:center}
#flow-supplier ol.clean li::before{background:var(--blue)}
#flow-tsm ol.clean li::before{background:var(--amber)}
#flow-wh ol.clean li::before{background:#3D6B9A}
ol.clean b{color:var(--ink)}
ul.clean{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none;display:grid;gap:8px;color:var(--ink-2)}
ul.clean li{padding-left:16px;border-left:3px solid var(--accent)}
ul.clean b{color:var(--ink)}
footer{margin-top:28px;color:#fff;font-size:13px;background:var(--accent-deep);border-radius:12px;padding:14px 18px}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="wrap">

<header>
  <div class="logo-plate"><img class="logo" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Byufuel"></div>
  <p class="eyebrow">Product guide</p>
  <h1>How Byufuel works</h1>
  <p class="lede">Used cooking oil is picked up from a restaurant, checked in at a warehouse, and the restaurant is paid.</p>
  <p class="lede">Read this page in order: what the product is, how a trip runs, how to set it up, who is involved, what QA tested, and what is still broken.</p>
  <p class="meta">QA · Rohan Bhagat · 22–29 Sep 2026 · Azure UAT</p>
</header>
<nav class="toc" aria-label="Contents">
  <a href="#product">Product</a>
  <a href="#flow">Flow</a>
  <a href="#flow-supplier">Supplier request</a>
  <a href="#flow-admin">Admin request</a>
  <a href="#flow-tsm">TSM</a>
  <a href="#flow-wh">Warehouse</a>
  <a href="#setup">Setup</a>
  <a href="#users">Users</a>
  <a href="#tested">What we tested</a>
  <a href="#failing">What is failing</a>
  <a href="#gaps">Gaps and issues</a>
  <a href="#creds">Creds and URLs</a>
  <a href="https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mISpkkLGxkkxxp4H9bprnaL_vt_aucMO" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Product documents</a>
</nav>

<section id="product">
  <h2>Product</h2>
  <p class="sec-sub">Byufuel collects used cooking oil from a restaurant, moves it to a warehouse in a scanned container, and pays the restaurant after the warehouse confirms the oil. One trip is three records that must stay linked: a bulk request, a schedule, and an itinerary.</p>
  <div class="tbl">
    <table>
      <thead><tr><th>Record</th><th>What it means</th><th>Example from the last run</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Bulk request (BR)</td><td>Admin asks for pickups for one or more suppliers. It stays pending until the job turns it into schedules.</td><td>BR-000000053 · 29 Sep · 10 kg · Hyderabad</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Schedule (SCH)</td><td>One restaurant, one date, one time slot, one weight and grade. This is the pickup the driver will visit.</td><td>SCH-000001680 · test 21 · Grade A · ₹101 · APPROVED</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Itinerary (IT)</td><td>The driver’s trip. It has a start, a drop warehouse, and the schedules to collect. Accept appears only after this record is Driver Assigned.</td><td>IT-000000312 · start Driver · drop Kukatpally Warehouse</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Container</td><td>The drum the oil goes in. The warehouse scans its QR, then sets the container count, the actual weight, and the final grade.</td><td>Closed loop used B-2609-3-00005. IT-312 was not scanned.</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
  <div class="tbl">
    <table>
      <thead><tr><th>Who</th><th>Where they work</th><th>Their job, in order</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Admin</td><td>Website</td><td>Creates the warehouse, slots, and grade rates. Creates a bulk request or approves a Sell Oil request, builds the itinerary, and assigns the driver. After check-in, approves or rejects a final grade of B or C. A reject sends the oil out with a different driver. Pays the restaurant: final count × base rate.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Supplier</td><td>Restaurant phone app</td><td>The restaurant. Raises Sell Oil itself, is selected by admin on a bulk request, or sees a pickup the TSM added. Gets paid after the oil is verified. Does not scan the container at the warehouse.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Driver</td><td>Driver phone app</td><td>Sees the trip under Upcoming, taps Accept, then Start, scans the container at the restaurant, signs the challan, and marks arrival at the warehouse.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Warehouse worker</td><td>Warehouse app</td><td>Scans the container QR, reads the QR details, sets the container count, updates the actual weight, and selects the final grade. If the oil is bad, the count is 0 and the container is marked bad. Does not drive to the restaurant.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>TSM</td><td>Field phone app only. No website.</td><td>Creates a prospect, records a visit, signs up a supplier, and can raise Sell Oil for suppliers in the assigned PIN codes. That pickup is flagged as created by the TSM. One supplier has one TSM.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Area lead</td><td>View only</td><td>Watches the TSMs who report to them, and the requests in those PIN codes. Does not create a prospect, a supplier, or a pickup.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>City lead</td><td>View only</td><td>Watches the area leads and TSMs under them, and the requests in those PIN codes. Does not create a prospect, a supplier, or a pickup. An area lead reports to a city lead. A city lead reports to an admin.</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
  <div class="callout">
    <strong>Current site</strong>
    <p>Web <a href="https://u-byufuel.azurewebsites.net">u-byufuel.azurewebsites.net</a> version 1.0.0 (20260922.1). API <code>https://u-byufuel-api.azurewebsites.net</code>. Driver and TSM phone app: <code>com.byufuel.uat</code>, which calls that same API. Area lead and city lead are view-only on that app. The older supplier app <code>com.byufuel.mobile</code> calls <code>d-byufuel-api</code>, so an Azure UAT driver is rejected there as unregistered. The old ngrok and Cloudflare tunnels are down and are not this environment.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="flow">
  <h2>Flow</h2>
  <p class="sec-sub">A pickup can start from the supplier, from admin, or from the TSM. After a schedule exists, the driver and the warehouse finish the trip the same way.</p>
  <nav class="subtoc" aria-label="Flows">
    <a href="#flow-supplier">Supplier creates the request</a>
    <a href="#flow-admin">Admin creates the request</a>
    <a href="#flow-tsm">TSM</a>
    <a href="#flow-wh">Warehouse check-in</a>
  </nav>
  <div class="phase" id="flow-supplier">
    <p class="kicker">Flow 1 · Restaurant phone app</p>
    <h3>Supplier creates the request</h3>
    <p class="sec-sub">The restaurant asks for the pickup. This does not start as a bulk request. Admin only approves it, then builds the trip.</p>
    <div class="flow">
      <div class="lane">
        <div class="lane-name">Supplier request</div>
        <div class="steps">
          <div class="step"><b>1. Sign in</b><span>Supplier opens the phone app.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>2. Sell Oil</b><span>Choose Pickup. Drop is a different menu.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>3. Book</b><span>Date, time slot, grade, weight. Submit.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>4. Schedule</b><span>A SCH is created as Request Placed.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>5. Admin approves</b><span>Manage Requests. Status becomes Approved.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>6. Trip</b><span>Itinerary, assign, collect, check in, pay.</span></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Sign in</b> on the supplier app. On the dev app that is <code>com.byufuel.mobile</code> as QA Supplier. An Azure UAT supplier such as test 21 was not signed in for the 29 Sep trip.</li>
      <li><b>Sell Oil → Pickup.</b> Do not use Drop unless the restaurant is bringing the oil to the warehouse itself.</li>
      <li><b>Fill the booking.</b> Date today or the next bookable day. A wide slot. Grade A. Weight, for example 10 kg. The estimate follows that area’s Grade A rate.</li>
      <li><b>Submit.</b> Note the schedule id. Status is Request Placed, not Approved yet.</li>
      <li><b>Admin approves</b> it under Manage Requests.</li>
      <li><b>Then the shared trip starts:</b> new itinerary, assign the driver, driver collects, warehouse checks in, admin pays. Those steps are under Admin creates the request, from “Build the trip” onward.</li>
    </ol>
  </div>

  <div class="phase" id="flow-admin">
    <p class="kicker">Flow 2 · Azure website</p>
    <h3>Admin creates the request</h3>
    <p class="sec-sub">Admin picks a supplier who is already approved. The restaurant does not open the app. This is the 29 Sep path: BR-000000053 → SCH-000001680 → IT-000000312.</p>
    <div class="flow">
      <div class="lane">
        <div class="lane-name">Admin request</div>
        <div class="steps">
          <div class="step"><b>1. Sign in</b><span>Admin on the Azure UAT website.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>2. Bulk request</b><span>Pick supplier, date, slot, 10 kg. Stays Pending.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>3. Schedule job</b><span>Pending BR becomes an Approved SCH.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>4. Itinerary</b><span>Start is Driver. Drop is the warehouse.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step ok"><b>5. Assign</b><span>Click ASSIGN. Itinerary must say Driver Assigned.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>6. Collect</b><span>Driver Accept, Start, scan, arrive.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>7. Check in and pay</b><span>Warehouse verifies the oil. Admin credits the restaurant.</span></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <h3>Create the bulk request</h3>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Sign in</b> on <a href="https://u-byufuel.azurewebsites.net">u-byufuel.azurewebsites.net</a> as admin.</li>
      <li><b>Create Bulk Request.</b> Pick an already approved supplier. On 29 Sep that was test 21.</li>
      <li><b>Fill the dialog.</b> Date <code>29/09/2026</code> (the screen shows 29-Sep-2026). Slot <code>4 PM to 6 PM</code>. Oil type <code>UCO</code>. Weight <code>10</code> kg. Grade A.</li>
      <li><b>Save.</b> <code>POST /api/bulk-uco-schedule-requests</code> returns 201. The request stays <b>PENDING</b>. This is BR-000000053.</li>
      <li><b>Turn it into a schedule.</b> Call <code>GET /api/uco-schedules/create-bulk-request-uco-schedules</code> with the admin Bearer token from <code>localStorage</code> key <code>bf:access_token</code> (it is stored as a JSON string, so parse the quotes). The job completes and the schedule becomes <b>APPROVED</b>.</li>
      <li><b>Result.</b> SCH-000001680 for test 21, 10 kg, Grade A, ₹101, Hyderabad.</li>
    </ol>
  </div>

  <div class="phase">
    <p class="kicker">After a supplier, admin, or TSM request is approved</p>
    <h3>Schedule becomes an itinerary, then a driver is assigned</h3>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Itinerary Management → New Itinerary.</b></li>
      <li><b>Select the schedule card</b> SCH-000001680. Do not pick an older schedule.</li>
      <li><b>Starting location = Driver. Drop = Kukatpally Warehouse</b> (WH-000000022, 346/12 A Phase 3, Hyderabad 500072). On this page the first dropdown is page size (5/10/20/50). The next dropdown is the start. The one after that is the drop. Other drops on the list are Security Warehouse, Warehouse, and Test - Warehouse.</li>
      <li><b>Create.</b> Note the new id. On 29 Sep this was IT-000000312. Right after create the status is <b>Itinerary Created</b>, not Driver Assigned.</li>
      <li><b>Open that itinerary → Assign Driver.</b> Find Hyd Driver1 and click the <b>ASSIGN</b> chip on that row. It is a clickable chip, not a form button.</li>
      <li><b>The save is</b> <code>PATCH /api/uco-schedule-itineraries/{id}/update-assign-driver</code>. It must return 200 and the itinerary status must become <b>Driver Assigned</b>.</li>
      <li><b>Check both records.</b> If only the schedule says assigned and the itinerary is still Created, the driver app stays empty. Accept never appears.</li>
    </ol>
  </div>

  <div class="phase">
    <p class="kicker">Step 3 · Driver collects the oil</p>
    <h3>Accept, start, scan, sign, arrive</h3>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Open <code>com.byufuel.uat</code></b> and sign in as the assigned driver. Do not use <code>com.byufuel.mobile</code> for this trip.</li>
      <li><b>Upcoming</b> lists trips whose date is today or later and whose status is Assigned, Accepted, or Started. After the assign above, IT-000000312 shows an <b>Accept</b> button.</li>
      <li><b>Accept</b> the trip.</li>
      <li><b>Start.</b> This can be blocked by the used-oil setting <code>driverJourneyStart</code>. On Azure the settings page returns 403, so that rule cannot be changed there. Start was not tapped on IT-312.</li>
      <li><b>At the restaurant stop, Scan.</b> The QR must be JSON: <code>{"Code":"B-2609-3-00005"}</code>. A plain code is Invalid QR on the driver.</li>
      <li><b>Enter quantity and capacity.</b> Quantity must match the schedule (10 kg on these runs). Capacity must be at least that weight. Grade A. Add a photo if the screen asks.</li>
      <li><b>Documents.</b> Sign as driver and as the restaurant, then Generate the challan. Leave Paid to Supplier unchecked unless you are testing cash. The PDF then says Not Paid, which is expected.</li>
      <li><b>Finish the stop and go to the drop warehouse.</b> Mark <b>Arrived at warehouse</b>. Guide mode is optional and has crashed before.</li>
    </ol>
    <p class="sec-sub">This collect path was completed on 23 Sep on IT-000001188 with Atul Ugale and container B-2609-3-00005. On 29 Sep, IT-312 stopped at Accept on the phone. It was not started or scanned.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="phase" id="flow-wh">
    <p class="kicker">Step 4 · Warehouse app</p>
    <h3>Scan the QR, set the weight, select the final grade</h3>
    <p class="sec-sub">This is the warehouse path from the team flow. The worker scans the same QR the driver carried in.</p>
    <div class="flow">
      <div class="lane">
        <div class="lane-name">Warehouse check-in</div>
        <div class="steps">
          <div class="step"><b>1. QR arrives</b><span>Supplier or driver requested the pickup. The driver brings the container.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>2. Scan</b><span>Open the QR scanner on the container code.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>3. QR details</b><span>Read the code, then set the container count.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>4. Actual weight</b><span>Update the weight that arrived.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>5. Final grade</b><span>Select the grade. Bad oil is count 0 and the container is marked bad.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>6. Admin</b><span>Grade B or C needs approve or reject. Reject changes the driver and the scan repeats.</span></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <h3>What the 24 Sep website check-in used</h3>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Sign in on the website</b> as the warehouse worker. The phone app hangs for a worker who was registered as a web user.</li>
      <li><b>Open Check in Oil.</b> Do not open Collect Oil. Collect Oil is a different list and can mark the trip Missing.</li>
      <li><b>Open the itinerary</b> only after the driver status is Arrived at warehouse.</li>
      <li><b>Scan → Manual</b> (not the camera). In QR Code, type the <b>plain</b> container code, for example <code>B-2609-3-00005</code>. Do not paste the JSON. JSON on this screen can crash with <code>gradeIds</code>.</li>
      <li><b>Enter.</b> On the verify panel set quantity 10 and Grade A, then click <b>Verify and Checkin</b>. Scanned containers should move to 1/1 and check-in weight to 10 kg.</li>
      <li><b>Confirm Checkin.</b> Status becomes Verified and Validated.</li>
      <li><b>Complete.</b> The itinerary moves to Delivered at warehouse.</li>
    </ol>
    <p class="sec-sub">This path was proven on 24 Sep on the same IT-188. Stopping after Enter, without Verify and Checkin, leaves scanned at 0/1 and Confirm never becomes usable. IT-312 was not checked in.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="phase">
    <p class="kicker">Step 5 · Admin pays the restaurant</p>
    <h3>Payment only after the oil is verified</h3>
    <p class="sec-sub">The team flow prices the oil as final count × base rate, then the payment succeeds or fails. Admin also compares the QR count with the final count.</p>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Amount.</b> UCO value = final count × base rate. This uses the weight and grade the warehouse confirmed, not the weight on the original request.</li>
      <li><b>Open supplier payment</b> for the delivered itinerary.</li>
      <li><b>Credit the amount</b> that matches the priced oil. On the closed loop that was ₹1180 (10 kg at the Mumbai Grade A rate plus GST), paid as cash with a reference. Status becomes Credited.</li>
      <li><b>The 29 Sep Azure price was ₹101</b> for the same 10 kg Grade A, because Hyderabad’s rate is different. That trip was not paid, because it never reached the warehouse.</li>
    </ol>
  </div>

  <div class="callout warn">
    <strong>Two wrong turns on the collect and check-in steps</strong>
    <p>Collect Oil is not the warehouse step. Using it, or reusing an old container QR, leaves the trip as Missing. The driver app wants a JSON QR such as <code>{"Code":"B-…"}</code>. The warehouse screen wants that same code as plain text.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="phase" id="flow-tsm">
    <p class="kicker">Flow 3 · TSM phone app</p>
    <h3>TSM adds the restaurant, then can raise the pickup</h3>
    <p class="sec-sub">TSM is a mobile role with no website. Area lead and city lead only view the TSMs under them. They do not create the prospect or the pickup. The 28 Sep run was signed in as Rohan AreaLead on <code>com.byufuel.uat</code>. The TSM login is Rohan Bhagat.</p>
    <div class="flow">
      <div class="lane">
        <div class="lane-name">TSM · new restaurant</div>
        <div class="steps">
          <div class="step"><b>1. Sign in</b><span>TSM on the phone app. No web menu.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>2. Prospect</b><span>Name, email, phone, area, shop, address. Complete closes the visit.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>3. Visit</b><span>Record a visit on a prospect or supplier in the TSM PIN codes.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>4. Sign up</b><span>Create the supplier. That TSM is their only contact.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>5. Admin converts</b><span>Requested to Convert, then Converted to Supplier.</span></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="lane">
        <div class="lane-name">TSM · sell oil</div>
        <div class="steps">
          <div class="step"><b>1. Sell Oil</b><span>Search suppliers in the TSM PIN codes only.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>2. Supplier</b><span>Name, PIN, or shop. Their locations appear.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>3. Book</b><span>Date, slot, UCO grade, quantity. Not recurring.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>4. Estimate</b><span>Quantity × rate, tax in or out.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>5. Confirm</b><span>Admin sees that the TSM created this request.</span></div>
          <div class="arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
          <div class="step"><b>6. Supplier app</b><span>The restaurant sees this pickup with their other Sell Oil requests.</span></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Sign in</b> on <code>com.byufuel.uat</code> as the TSM. Rohan Bhagat is that login. The 28 Sep field run was Rohan AreaLead.</li>
      <li><b>Create a prospect.</b> First name, last name, email, phone, operational area, establishment name, address with latitude and longitude, and remarks are required. Follow-up date is optional. Complete marks the visit done. On 28 Sep, QA TSM Shop, contact QA TsmSep, <code>qa.tsm.prospect928@yopmail.com</code>, 9876501991, Pune 411009 was saved. The Visits tab shows that row.</li>
      <li><b>Record a visit</b> from the list of prospects and suppliers in the TSM PIN codes. On that run, home search did nothing, visit search said No data found, and the Prospect and Supplier tabs stayed empty.</li>
      <li><b>Sign up the supplier.</b> App usage, name, email, phone, operational area, establishment, and addresses. The supplier is linked to this TSM. One supplier has one TSM. On that run the form stopped at the phone OTP, so the supplier was not created.</li>
      <li><b>Admin converts the prospect.</b> Open the prospect in Requested to Convert, approve it, and the status becomes Converted to Supplier. Sell Oil is then available for that supplier.</li>
      <li><b>Raise Sell Oil.</b> Search by name, PIN, or establishment, only inside the TSM PIN codes. Pick a location, date, slot, UCO grade, and quantity. Recurring is not offered. Confirm. The supplier app lists that pickup with the restaurant’s other requests.</li>
      <li><b>Then the shared trip starts:</b> itinerary, assign the driver, collect, warehouse check-in, pay.</li>
      <li><b>Area lead and city lead</b> only view the TSMs under them and the requests in those PIN codes. Rohan AreaLead reports to Rohan CityLead. Rohan CityLead reports to Hyd Admin.</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="setup">
  <h2>Setup</h2>
  <p class="sec-sub">Do this once before the first pickup. If any of these is missing, the later steps fail in a confusing way: empty Upcoming, Start blocked, or a price of zero.</p>
  <div class="phase">
    <p class="kicker">Where to work</p>
    <h3>Use one environment for the whole trip</h3>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Website</b> <a href="https://u-byufuel.azurewebsites.net">https://u-byufuel.azurewebsites.net</a></li>
      <li><b>API</b> <code>https://u-byufuel-api.azurewebsites.net</code></li>
      <li><b>Phone app for driver and TSM</b> <code>com.byufuel.uat</code>. It must call the UAT API above. Area lead and city lead are view-only on the same app.</li>
      <li><b>Supplier on the older phone build</b> <code>com.byufuel.mobile</code> calls <code>d-byufuel-api</code>. That is a different database. A user created on UAT will not sign in there.</li>
      <li><b>Registration channel matters.</b> Supplier and driver are mobile users, so they sign in on the app. A warehouse worker created as a web user signs in on the website. The same web user hangs on the phone app.</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="phase">
    <p class="kicker">Master data</p>
    <h3>What admin must have before Create Bulk Request</h3>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Operational area.</b> 29 Sep used Hyderabad. The closed loop on 23–24 Sep used Mumbai (<code>MUM001</code>). Pick the area that matches the supplier and the warehouse.</li>
      <li><b>Warehouse.</b> 29 Sep drop was Kukatpally Warehouse, code WH-000000022. The closed loop drop was WareOne, code WH-000000046. The driver drop list and the warehouse worker must point at the same warehouse.</li>
      <li><b>Time slots.</b> Create at least one slot the supplier or bulk form can pick. Empty slots have returned HTTP 500 on time-slot search. The bulk form shows clock labels such as 4 PM to 6 PM. The master slot screen still shows hour numbers 1–24.</li>
      <li><b>A rate for each grade in that area.</b> The warehouse payment is final count × base rate. The TSM estimate is quantity × rate, with tax included or excluded. Mumbai Grade A was ₹100/kg + 18% GST, so 10 kg = ₹1180. Hyderabad on 29 Sep priced 10 kg Grade A at ₹101. On Azure the grade dropdown only lists Grade A, so B and C cannot be priced there.</li>
      <li><b>Used-oil configuration.</b> This page should set minimum and maximum kg, currency, grades, and whether the driver may press Start (<code>driverJourneyStart</code>). On Azure UAT the menu is missing and the page returns 403, so Start rules cannot be changed there.</li>
      <li><b>One unused container.</b> Generate a new QR from admin before the driver collects. Generate QR asks for a count and a warehouse. It creates a new code. It does not attach a QR to a container that already exists. Never reuse a code from an older trip.</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="phase">
    <p class="kicker">People</p>
    <h3>Who must already be active</h3>
    <ol class="clean">
      <li><b>Supplier</b> status Active, in the same city as the request. Bulk request only lists approved suppliers.</li>
      <li><b>Driver</b> status Active, with a vehicle, in that operational area. Assign uses this driver. A driver stuck at Registered, or missing KYC and vehicle documents, cannot be approved. Approve then returns HTTP 500.</li>
      <li><b>Warehouse worker</b> linked to the drop warehouse, able to open the website.</li>
      <li><b>Admin</b> who can create requests, itineraries, and payments, and who approves a final grade of B or C.</li>
      <li><b>TSM</b> on the phone app, with PIN codes, if the restaurant is found in the field or the TSM raises Sell Oil.</li>
      <li><b>Area lead and city lead</b> only if someone needs to view those TSMs. They do not have to be active for the pickup itself.</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="failing">
  <h2>What is failing</h2>
  <p class="sec-sub">These are the breaks a developer will hit if they follow the flow above. Each one was seen with a signed-in user.</p>
  <div class="tbl">
    <table>
      <thead><tr><th>Where</th><th>What the person does</th><th>What happens</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Sign up</td><td>Fills the restaurant form</td><td>No address, map, or bank fields. No Verify or Send OTP. An existing email or phone sticks on the logo.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Password</td><td>Sets a weak password, or resets with the emailed code</td><td>A weak or mismatched password is not rejected. Forgot-password shows a broken <code>{name}</code> / <code>{id}</code> message and does not change the password.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Bank</td><td>Types IFSC <code>BAD123</code></td><td>No format error. A bad submit is not clearly rejected.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Sell oil</td><td>Books a slot with no weight</td><td>Nothing happens. There is no alert. Drop still cannot select a warehouse.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>New supplier email</td><td>Admin creates the account</td><td>The account is created. The inbox stays empty.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Used-oil settings</td><td>Admin opens UCO Configuration</td><td>No menu item. The page returns 403.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Rates</td><td>Admin opens the grade list</td><td>Only Grade A. Grade B and Grade C cannot be priced.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>QR</td><td>Admin generates a code</td><td>The form asks for a count and a warehouse only. It does not attach a code to an existing container.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Driver scan vs warehouse</td><td>Someone scans the container</td><td>The driver rejects a plain code. The warehouse wants the plain code. JSON on the warehouse screen can crash the page.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Driver trip</td><td>Looks for Cancel, or opens Collect Oil</td><td>Cancel is missing. The only action is Raise a Ticket. Collect Oil can mark the trip Missing, and then Scan is hidden.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Weekly pickup</td><td>Admin creates a second weekly request</td><td>No confirmation. A second request is created.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Statuses</td><td>Compares incoming deliveries with the driver trip</td><td>The website can say Driver Assigned while the driver trip says Driver Accepted. Time slots are numbers in one screen and clock labels in another.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Chat</td><td>Opens chat while already signed in</td><td>Session error 401. Chat does not stay connected.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Driver approval</td><td>Approves a driver with no KYC</td><td>HTTP 500 instead of a clear message. A supplier can still be set Active with empty KYC and bank.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Warehouse app</td><td>A web warehouse worker signs in on the phone</td><td>The app hangs. The same person can use the website.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>TSM app</td><td>Searches for the shop just saved</td><td>Search does nothing. Prospect and Supplier tabs stay empty. Supplier create stops at the phone code.</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="gaps">
  <h2>Gaps and issues</h2>
  <p class="sec-sub">Same findings, grouped as the open product list. The live copy is the Key issues and Gaps tab. Doubts were left as they were.</p>
  <div class="tbl">
    <table>
      <thead><tr><th></th><th>Gap</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td class="num">1</td><td>Used-oil settings page is blocked (403).</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">2</td><td>Only Grade A can be priced.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">3</td><td>QR cannot be tied to an existing container, and the driver and warehouse expect different code formats.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">4</td><td>Driver cannot cancel a pickup.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">5</td><td>Collect Oil is the wrong path and can leave the trip Missing.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">6</td><td>Start can still be blocked by the used-oil setting, and that settings page cannot be opened.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">7</td><td>Replacing a weekly pickup does not ask for confirmation.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">8</td><td>A new supplier does not get a registration email.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">9</td><td>Time-slot labels and delivery status text do not match across screens.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">10</td><td>Sign up is missing address, map, bank, and OTP, and submit can stick on the logo.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">11</td><td>Password rules and forgot-password do not finish correctly.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">12</td><td>Bank IFSC and invalid bank details are not clearly rejected.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">13</td><td>Booking with no weight gives no warning. Reports have no month or quarter picker.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">14</td><td>Chat returns 401. A driver with no KYC cannot be approved. The warehouse phone app hangs.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">15</td><td>TSM search, Prospect tab, and Supplier tab do not show the shop that was just saved.</td><td><span class="pill p-fail">Open</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">16</td><td>UCO Pickup had no trip because the tunnel was down.</td><td><span class="pill p-pass">Closed</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">17</td><td>Price showed 0.00, supplier could not be created, and Assign did not show Accept.</td><td><span class="pill p-pass">Closed</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="num">18</td><td>Warehouse check-in could not finish. The plain-code path now verifies and pays.</td><td><span class="pill p-pass">Closed</span></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
